title: A counterexample to global convergence of classical DFP under the standard strong Wolfe conditions
summary: A long-standing open question in quasi-Newton optimization asks whether the classical Davidon--Fletcher--Powell (DFP) method converges globally on uniformly convex objectives when all accepted steps satisfy the standard weak Wolfe conditions. We show that the answer is no, even under the standard strong Wolfe conditions. Fix $0<c_1<2/3$ and $2/3\le c_2<1$. We construct a function $f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ such that $\frac{1}{2}I\preceq\nabla^2 f(x)\preceq\frac{3}{2}I$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^2$.
